import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Eden's conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Eden's conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden%27s_conjecture)
- [N. Kuznetsov, *The Lyapunov dimension and its estimation via the Leonov method*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05410)
-/

open Filter Set
open scoped InnerProduct NNReal

namespace EdensConjecture

/-- A compact invariant set is a global attractor if it is nonempty and attracts every bounded
set in the one-sided Hausdorff semidistance. -/
def IsGlobalAttractor {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 X)
    (K : Set X) : Prop :=
  K.Nonempty ∧ IsCompact K ∧ (∀ t, φ t '' K = K) ∧
    ∀ B : Set X, Bornology.IsBounded B →
      Tendsto (fun t ↦ ⨆ x : B, ENNReal.ofReal (Metric.infDist (φ t x) K)) atTop (nhds 0)

/-- The singular values of an endomorphism of Euclidean `n`-space, in decreasing order. -/
noncomputable def singularValue {n : ℕ}
    (A : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt ((ContinuousLinearMap.isPositive_adjoint_comp_self A).isSymmetric.eigenvalues
    finrank_euclideanSpace_fin i)

/-- The singular-value function $\omega_d(A)$, with linear interpolation in its order `d`. -/
noncomputable def singularValueFunction {n : ℕ}
    (A : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (d : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n, singularValue A i ^ (min 1 (max 0 (d - i)))

/-- Eden's infinite-time local Lyapunov dimension.  It uses the limsup of the `t`-th roots of
$\omega_d(D\varphi^t(u))$ and takes the critical order at which this growth is less than one. -/
noncomputable def localLyapunovDimension {n : ℕ}
    (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) : ℝ :=
  sInf (insert (n : ℝ) {d : ℝ | d ∈ Icc 0 (n : ℝ) ∧
    limsup (fun t : ℝ≥0 ↦ ENNReal.ofReal
      (singularValueFunction (fderiv ℝ (φ t) u) d) ^ (1 / (t : ℝ))) atTop < 1})

/-- **Eden's conjecture.** For every smooth finite-dimensional dynamical system with compact
global attractor $K$, the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions on $K$ is attained at a
point of $K$ which is either stationary or lies on a periodic orbit contained in $K$.  No
additional instability condition is imposed on the periodic orbit. -/
@[category research open, AMS 34 37]
theorem edens_conjecture (n : ℕ) (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))
    (K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (hφ : ∀ t, ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (φ t))
    (hK : IsGlobalAttractor φ K) :
    ∃ u ∈ K, ((∀ t, φ t u = u) ∨ ∃ T : ℝ≥0, 0 < T ∧ φ T u = u) ∧
      localLyapunovDimension φ u = sSup (localLyapunovDimension φ '' K) := by
  sorry

end EdensConjecture
modeling_decisions: Modeled a smooth finite-dimensional dynamical system as a jointly continuous semiflow `Flow ℝ≥0` on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`, with every fixed-time map required to be `ContDiff ℝ ⊤`.
Defined a global attractor to be nonempty, compact, strictly invariant (`φ t '' K = K`), and attracting every bounded set in the standard one-sided Hausdorff semidistance.

Used Eden's infinite-time local Lyapunov dimension: singular values are those of the Fréchet derivative, `ω_d` is the interpolated singular-value product, and the asymptotic growth is the limsup of `(ω_d(Dφ^t(u)))^(1/t)`. The critical-order definition is the equivalent singular-value formulation of the Kaplan–Yorke dimension; inserting `n` implements the source's convention that the value is `n` when the defining set is empty.

Interpreted a stationary point as one fixed for every nonnegative time, and membership in a periodic orbit as return after some strictly positive time. Strict invariance of `K` ensures that the resulting orbit is embedded in `K`.
Following the fixed decomposition guidance, did not impose an instability hypothesis on the periodic orbit; this preserves stable-equilibrium and stable-cycle degenerate cases.
Expressed attainment as equality with `sSup (localLyapunovDimension φ '' K)`, not merely as approximation to the supremum.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Eden's conjecture

Eden's conjecture states that the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions on the global
attractor of a smooth dynamical system is achieved on a stationary point or an (unstable)
periodic orbit embedded into the attractor.

We consider a smooth dynamical system in $\mathbb{R}^n$ generated by an autonomous differential
equation $\dot u = f(u)$ with $f$ continuously differentiable, all of whose solutions exist for
$t \in [0, \infty)$. Its evolutionary operator $\varphi^t$ is a $C^1$ semigroup. Let
$\sigma_1(t,u) \ge \dots \ge \sigma_n(t,u)$ be the singular values of the fundamental matrix
$D\varphi^t(u)$ and $\omega_k(D\varphi^t(u)) = \sigma_1(t,u) \cdots \sigma_k(t,u)$ the singular
value function of order $k$ (with $\omega_0 = 1$).

Following Eden (1989), the *local Lyapunov exponents* $\mu_1(u), \dots, \mu_n(u)$ at a point $u$
are defined through their partial sums
$$\mu_1(u) + \dots + \mu_k(u) = \limsup_{t \to +\infty} \frac{1}{t} \ln \omega_k(D\varphi^t(u)),$$
and the *local Lyapunov dimension* at $u$ is given by the Kaplan–Yorke formula
$$\dim_{\rm L}(u) = j + \frac{\mu_1(u) + \dots + \mu_j(u)}{|\mu_{j+1}(u)|},$$
where $j = j(u)$ is the largest integer with $\mu_1(u) + \dots + \mu_j(u) \ge 0$ (and
$\dim_{\rm L}(u) = n$ if $j = n$).

A *global attractor* of the system is a nonempty compact set $K$ that is invariant
($\varphi^t(K) = K$ for all $t \ge 0$) and attracts every bounded set. Eden's conjecture asserts
that there is a point $u \in K$ that is either a stationary point or lies on a periodic orbit,
at which $\dim_{\rm L}(u) = \sup_{v \in K} \dim_{\rm L}(v)$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- A. Eden, *An abstract theory of L-exponents with applications to dimension analysis*, PhD thesis,
  Indiana University, 1989 (p. 98, Question 1).
- A. Eden, *Local Lyapunov exponents and a local estimate of Hausdorff dimension*, Modélisation
  Mathématique et Analyse Numérique 23 (1989), 405–413.
- N. V. Kuznetsov, *The Lyapunov dimension and its estimation via the Leonov method*, Physics
  Letters A 380 (2016), 2142–2149, [arXiv:1602.05410](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05410).
-/

open Filter Set Topology

namespace EdensConjecture

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The Euclidean phase space $\mathbb{R}^n$. -/
local notation "E" => EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)

/-- The singular values $\sigma_1(A) \ge \sigma_2(A) \ge \dots \ge \sigma_n(A) \ge 0$ of a linear
map `A` on $\mathbb{R}^n$, i.e. the square roots of the eigenvalues of the symmetric operator
$A^* A$, listed in decreasing order. -/
noncomputable def singularValues (A : E →L[ℝ] E) : Fin n → ℝ := fun i =>
  Real.sqrt ((LinearMap.isSymmetric_adjoint_mul_self (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E)).eigenvalues
    finrank_euclideanSpace_fin i)

/-- The singular value function of integer order `k` of a linear map `A` on $\mathbb{R}^n$:
$\omega_k(A) = \sigma_1(A) \cdots \sigma_k(A)$ for $1 \le k \le n$, and $\omega_0(A) = 1$. -/
noncomputable def singularValueFunction (A : E →L[ℝ] E) (k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n with i.val < k, singularValues A i

/-- `φ` is the evolutionary operator (forward flow) of the autonomous differential equation
$\dot u = f(u)$: for every initial point `u`, the curve $t \mapsto \varphi^t(u)$, $t \ge 0$,
is the solution starting at `u`. Since `f` is assumed to be $C^1$ in the conjecture, this solution
is unique, so `φ t` is determined by `f` for `t ≥ 0`. -/
structure IsEvolutionOperator (f : E → E) (φ : ℝ → E → E) : Prop where
  map_zero : ∀ u, φ 0 u = u
  hasDerivWithinAt : ∀ u, ∀ t, 0 ≤ t →
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun s => φ s u) (f (φ t u)) (Ici 0) t

/-- `K` is the global attractor of the dynamical system `φ`: a nonempty compact set which is
invariant, $\varphi^t(K) = K$ for all $t \ge 0$, and which attracts every bounded set `B`, i.e.
$\sup_{b \in B} \operatorname{dist}(\varphi^t(b), K) \to 0$ as $t \to +\infty$. -/
structure IsGlobalAttractor (φ : ℝ → E → E) (K : Set E) : Prop where
  nonempty : K.Nonempty
  isCompact : IsCompact K
  invariant : ∀ t, 0 ≤ t → φ t '' K = K
  attracts : ∀ B : Set E, Bornology.IsBounded B → ∀ ε > 0, ∃ T, ∀ t ≥ T, ∀ b ∈ B,
    Metric.infDist (φ t b) K < ε

/-- The sum $\mu_1(u) + \dots + \mu_k(u)$ of the first `k` local Lyapunov exponents of the
dynamical system `φ` at the point `u`, in the sense of Eden:
$$\mu_1(u) + \dots + \mu_k(u) = \limsup_{t \to +\infty} \frac{1}{t} \ln \omega_k(D\varphi^t(u)),$$
where $D\varphi^t(u)$ is the derivative of $\varphi^t$ at `u`. -/
noncomputable def localLyapunovExponentSum (φ : ℝ → E → E) (u : E) (k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  limsup (fun t : ℝ => Real.log (singularValueFunction (fderiv ℝ (φ t) u) k) / t) atTop

/-- The local Lyapunov dimension of the dynamical system `φ` at the point `u`, given by the
Kaplan–Yorke formula applied to Eden's local Lyapunov exponents:
$$\dim_{\rm L}(u) = j + \frac{\mu_1(u) + \dots + \mu_j(u)}{|\mu_{j+1}(u)|},$$
where $j$ is the largest integer in $\{0, \dots, n\}$ with $\mu_1(u) + \dots + \mu_j(u) \ge 0$,
and $\dim_{\rm L}(u) = n$ if $j = n$. -/
noncomputable def localLyapunovDimension (φ : ℝ → E → E) (u : E) : ℝ :=
  let Λ := localLyapunovExponentSum φ u
  let j := Nat.findGreatest (fun k => 0 ≤ Λ k) n
  if j = n then n else j + Λ j / |Λ (j + 1) - Λ j|

/-- The singular values are listed in decreasing order. -/
@[category API, AMS 15]
theorem singularValues_antitone (A : E →L[ℝ] E) : Antitone (singularValues A) :=
  fun _ _ hij => Real.sqrt_le_sqrt (LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues_antitone _ _ hij)

/-- The singular value function of order `0` is identically `1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 15]
theorem singularValueFunction_zero (A : E →L[ℝ] E) : singularValueFunction A 0 = 1 := by
  simp [singularValueFunction]

/-- The empty sum of local Lyapunov exponents is `0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 37]
theorem localLyapunovExponentSum_zero (φ : ℝ → E → E) (u : E) :
    localLyapunovExponentSum φ u 0 = 0 := by
  simp [localLyapunovExponentSum, singularValueFunction_zero]

/-- The local Lyapunov dimension takes values in $[0, n]$. -/
@[category API, AMS 37]
theorem localLyapunovDimension_mem_Icc (φ : ℝ → E → E) (u : E) :
    localLyapunovDimension φ u ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) n := by
  simp only [localLyapunovDimension]
  set Λ := localLyapunovExponentSum φ u
  set j := Nat.findGreatest (fun k => 0 ≤ Λ k) n with hj
  have hjn : j ≤ n := Nat.findGreatest_le n
  split_ifs with h
  · exact ⟨by positivity, le_rfl⟩
  · have hΛj : 0 ≤ Λ j := Nat.findGreatest_spec (P := fun k => 0 ≤ Λ k) (Nat.zero_le n)
      (by simp [Λ, localLyapunovExponentSum_zero])
    have hlt : j < n := lt_of_le_of_ne hjn h
    have hΛj1 : Λ (j + 1) < 0 := by
      have := Nat.findGreatest_is_greatest (P := fun k => 0 ≤ Λ k) (Nat.lt_succ_self j) hlt
      simpa using this
    have hden : 0 < |Λ (j + 1) - Λ j| := abs_pos.mpr (by linarith)
    have hratio : Λ j / |Λ (j + 1) - Λ j| < 1 := by
      rw [div_lt_one hden, abs_of_neg (by linarith)]
      linarith
    refine ⟨by positivity, ?_⟩
    have : (j : ℝ) + 1 ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hlt
    linarith

/-- The map $(t, u) \mapsto e^{-t} u$ is the evolutionary operator of $\dot u = -u$. -/
@[category test, AMS 37]
theorem isEvolutionOperator_exp_neg_smul :
    IsEvolutionOperator (fun u : E => -u) (fun t u => Real.exp (-t) • u) where
  map_zero u := by simp
  hasDerivWithinAt u t _ := by
    have := ((hasDerivAt_neg t).exp).smul_const (F := E) u
    simpa [neg_smul] using this.hasDerivWithinAt

/-- The origin is the global attractor of the linear system $\dot u = -u$. -/
@[category test, AMS 37]
theorem isGlobalAttractor_exp_neg_smul :
    IsGlobalAttractor (fun t (u : E) => Real.exp (-t) • u) {0} where
  nonempty := ⟨0, rfl⟩
  isCompact := isCompact_singleton
  invariant t _ := by simp
  attracts B hB ε hε := by
    obtain ⟨R, hR⟩ := hB.subset_closedBall 0
    obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ : ∃ T : ℝ, ∀ t ≥ T, Real.exp (-t) * R < ε := by
      have : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => Real.exp (-t) * R) atTop (𝓝 (0 * R)) :=
        (Real.tendsto_exp_neg_atTop_nhds_zero).mul_const R
      rw [zero_mul] at this
      exact (this.eventually (gt_mem_nhds hε)).exists_forall_of_atTop
    refine ⟨T, fun t ht b hb => ?_⟩
    rw [Metric.infDist_singleton, dist_zero_right, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs,
      abs_of_pos (Real.exp_pos _)]
    have hb' : ‖b‖ ≤ R := by simpa using hR hb
    calc Real.exp (-t) * ‖b‖ ≤ Real.exp (-t) * R := by gcongr
      _ < ε := hT t ht

/--
**Eden's conjecture.** Let $\dot u = f(u)$ be an autonomous differential equation in
$\mathbb{R}^n$ with $f$ continuously differentiable, whose solutions exist for all $t \ge 0$, and
let $\varphi^t$ be its evolutionary operator. If $K$ is the global attractor of the system, then
the supremum $\sup_{v \in K} \dim_{\rm L}(v)$ of the local Lyapunov dimensions on $K$ is achieved
at a point $u \in K$ which is a stationary point ($\varphi^t(u) = u$ for all $t \ge 0$) or lies on
a periodic orbit ($\varphi^T(u) = u$ for some $T > 0$) embedded into $K$.

The word "unstable" in the informal statement is descriptive (a periodic orbit inside a chaotic
attractor is necessarily unstable) and is not imposed as a hypothesis.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 37]
theorem edens_conjecture (f : E → E) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) (φ : ℝ → E → E)
    (hφ : IsEvolutionOperator f φ) (K : Set E) (hK : IsGlobalAttractor φ K) :
    ∃ u ∈ K, ((∀ t, 0 ≤ t → φ t u = u) ∨ ∃ T > 0, φ T u = u) ∧
      ∀ v ∈ K, localLyapunovDimension φ v ≤ localLyapunovDimension φ u := by
  sorry

end EdensConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: Minor: Eden posed the question (thesis 1989, p. 98, Question 1) for abstract semigroups on Hilbert spaces with compact global attractors (the article cites its verification for the complex Ginzburg–Landau equation, an infinite-dimensional system), whereas the table fixes 'smooth finite-dimensional dynamical systems'. The formalization conforms to the table; the finite-dimensional statement is a special case of the general question. The table's phrase 'Kaplan–Yorke formula applied to the limsup ... local Lyapunov exponents' was followed; note that Kuznetsov's paper also writes Eden's local dimension in the equivalent-in-good-cases form inf{d : limsup (1/t) ln ω_d < 0}, which may differ from the Kaplan–Yorke value in degenerate non-concave situations.
modeling_decisions: Dynamical system class: continuous-time systems generated by an autonomous ODE u̇ = f(u) in R^n with f ∈ C^1 and all solutions existing for t ≥ 0 (Kuznetsov arXiv:1602.05410 §2 setup, Eden's finite-dimensional setting). Discrete-time maps and Eden's original infinite-dimensional (Hilbert-space semigroup) setting are not covered, per the decomposition notes fixing 'smooth finite-dimensional dynamical systems'.

The flow is given as a function φ : ℝ → E → E constrained only for t ≥ 0 (HasDerivWithinAt on Ici 0); values at negative times are irrelevant junk (every use of φ in the statement involves t ≥ 0, T > 0, or t → +∞).

Global attractor = nonempty compact set, strictly invariant (φ^t K = K, t ≥ 0), attracting all bounded sets uniformly (Temam/Eden definition). Kuznetsov et al. sometimes use 'minimal set attracting all points' instead; the two can differ, and the Temam definition (Eden's framework) was chosen. K.Nonempty is explicit because Metric.infDist x ∅ = 0 in Lean.

Local Lyapunov dimension is Eden's infinite-time version: Kaplan–Yorke formula on the limsup local exponents (partial sums Λ_k(u) = limsup (1/t) ln ω_k(Dφ^t u)), with j = largest k ≤ n such that Λ_k ≥ 0 (the literal Kaplan–Yorke wording; coincides with the first sign change when k ↦ Λ_k is concave). Kuznetsov's alternative form inf{d ∈ [0,n] : limsup (1/t) ln ω_d(Dφ^t u) < 0} with real-order ω_d can in principle differ when the limsups are not attained along a common sequence; the notes prescribe the Kaplan–Yorke form.

The limsup is taken in ℝ (Filter.limsup on atTop). For u in a compact invariant set of a C^1 ODE flow, (1/t) ln ω_k(Dφ^t u) is bounded (|·| ≤ k·sup_K ‖Df‖), so no junk value is reached at the points where the statement evaluates the dimension.

'Stationary point or periodic orbit embedded into the attractor' is formalized as u ∈ K with (∀ t ≥ 0, φ t u = u) ∨ (∃ T > 0, φ T u = u); 'unstable' is not imposed (per notes), and the whole orbit lies in K by invariance.
'Supremum achieved' is formalized as ∀ v ∈ K, dim_L(v) ≤ dim_L(u) for the witness u, avoiding sSup/iSup conventions and forcing actual attainment.
Dφ^t(u) is taken as fderiv ℝ (φ t) u; differentiability of φ^t in u is a theorem of ODE theory for C^1 f and hence is not assumed.

$$\dim_{\mathrm L} u = \inf\{d \in [0, n] : \limsup_{t \to +\infty}
  \omega_d(D\varphi^t(u))^{1/t} < 1\},$$

- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden%27s_conjecture)

linear map $A : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$, in decreasing order: the square roots of the
eigenvalues of the positive symmetric operator $A^* A$. -/
noncomputable def singularValue (A : ℝ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ^n) (i : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt ((ContinuousLinearMap.isPositive_adjoint_comp_self A).isSymmetric.eigenvalues
    finrank_euclideanSpace_fin i)

$A : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$:
$$\omega_d(A) = \sigma_0(A) \cdots \sigma_{\lfloor d \rfloor - 1}(A)

    (1 : ℝ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ^n)).isSymmetric.eigenvalues finrank_euclideanSpace_fin i = μ at h ⊢

    RCLike.ofReal_real_eq_id] at h

    singularValueFunction (1 : ℝ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ^n) d = 1 := by
  simp [singularValueFunction, singularValue_one]

$$\dim_{\mathrm L} u = \inf\{d \in [0, n] : \limsup_{t \to +\infty}

singular value function of order $d$. If no such $d$ exists (no order of the linearisation is

  sInf (insert (n : ℝ) {d ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) n |
    limsup (fun t : ℝ≥0 =>
      ENNReal.ofReal (singularValueFunction (fderiv ℝ (φ t) u) d) ^ (1 / (t : ℝ))) atTop < 1})

theorem localLyapunovDimension_mem_Icc (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 (ℝ^n)) (u : ℝ^n) :
    localLyapunovDimension φ u ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) n := by

Discrete-time systems (iterates of a C^1 map), which Kuznetsov also treats, are NOT covered; the statement's wording ('stationary point', Eden's original setting) is continuous-time. No joint C^1-regularity in (t,u) and no invertibility of Dφ^t(u) is assumed (both hold automatically for ODE flows), so the class is slightly larger than ODE-generated systems.

Local Lyapunov dimension = Kuznetsov's displayed formula for Eden's infinite-time local dimension: dim_L(u) = inf{ d ∈ [0,n] : limsup_{t→∞} ω_d(Dφ^t(u))^{1/t} < 1 }, with d real inside ω_d and the convention dim = n when the set is empty (implemented as `sInf (insert n {...})`). This coincides with the Kaplan–Yorke formula applied to the limsup local Lyapunov exponents whenever the finite-time exponents converge (e.g. at equilibria and on periodic orbits), but the two can differ at points where they do not converge (the KY interpolation is ≥ this value). The limsup is taken in ℝ≥0∞ (via ENNReal.ofReal and ENNReal rpow) to avoid junk values; the multiplicative form ω_d^{1/t} < 1 is used instead of (1/t) log ω_d < 0 so that zero singular values (Real.log 0 = 0 junk) cause no problem.

def IsGlobalAttractor (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (K : Set E) : Prop :=
  IsCompact K ∧ (∀ t, φ t '' K = K) ∧
    ∀ B : Set E, Bornology.IsBounded B → ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ t in atTop, φ t '' B ⊆ Metric.thickening ε K

/-- The sum `μ₁(u) + ⋯ + μ_j(u)` of the first `j` local Lyapunov exponents (in the sense of Eden)
of the semiflow `φ` at the point `u`:
$$\mu_1(u) + \dots + \mu_j(u) = \limsup_{t \to +\infty} \frac{1}{t} \ln \omega_j(D\varphi^t(u)),$$
where `ω_j` is the singular value function of order `j`. The value is taken in `EReal`
(with `ln 0 = -∞`). -/
noncomputable def localLyapunovExponentSum (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (u : E) (j : ℕ) : EReal :=
  limsup (fun t : ℝ≥0 => (((t : ℝ)⁻¹ : ℝ) : EReal) *
    ENNReal.log (ENNReal.ofReal (singularValueFunction (fderiv ℝ (φ t) u : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) j))) atTop

/-- The local Lyapunov dimension `dim_L(u)` of the semiflow `φ` at the point `u`, obtained from
the local Lyapunov exponents `μ₁(u), …, μₙ(u)` at `u` by the Kaplan–Yorke formula:
$$\dim_{\rm L}(u) = j + \frac{\mu_1(u) + \dots + \mu_j(u)}{|\mu_{j+1}(u)|},$$
where `j` is the largest integer in `{0, …, n}` such that `μ₁(u) + ⋯ + μ_j(u) ≥ 0`, and

`s = d - ⌊d⌋`, of the partial sums of the local Lyapunov exponents is nonnegative. -/
noncomputable def localLyapunovDim (φ : Flow ℝ≥0 E) (u : E) : ℝ :=
  sSup {d : ℝ | d ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (Module.finrank ℝ E) ∧

theorem singularValueFunction_zero (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) : singularValueFunction A 0 = 1 := by

/-!
# Eden's conjecture

Eden's conjecture concerns where the largest local Lyapunov dimension on a global attractor is
attained. We use Eden's infinite-time local Lyapunov dimension, based on the asymptotic growth of
the singular-value functions of the spatial derivative of a smooth semiflow.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Eden's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden%27s_conjecture)
- [N. V. Kuznetsov, *The Lyapunov dimension and its estimation via the Leonov method*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05410)
-/

open Bornology Filter Set Topology
open scoped InnerProduct

namespace EdensConjecture

/-- The Euclidean phase space of dimension `n`. -/
abbrev PhaseSpace (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)

/-- The `i`th singular value, in decreasing order, of an endomorphism of `PhaseSpace n`.
It is the square root of the `i`th eigenvalue of the Gram operator $A^*A$. -/
noncomputable def singularValue {n : ℕ} (A : PhaseSpace n →L[ℝ] PhaseSpace n)
    (i : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt ((LinearMap.isSymmetric_adjoint_mul_self A.toLinearMap).eigenvalues (by simp) i)

/-- The singular-value function $\omega_d(A)$. For $j=\lfloor d\rfloor<n$, this is the
product of the first `j` singular values times the next singular value to the power $d-j$.
For $j\geq n$, it is the product of all `n` singular values. -/
noncomputable def singularValueFunction {n : ℕ} (A : PhaseSpace n →L[ℝ] PhaseSpace n)
    (d : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  let j := ⌊d⌋₊
  if h : j < n then
    (∏ i : Fin j, singularValue A (Fin.castLE h.le i)) *
      (singularValue A ⟨j, h⟩) ^ (d - j)
  else
    ∏ i : Fin n, singularValue A i

/-- A smooth finite-dimensional semiflow. The underlying `Flow NNReal` supplies the jointly
continuous action, identity at time zero, and semigroup law. Spatial time maps are smooth, and
their spatial derivatives depend continuously on time and state. -/
structure SmoothSemiflow (n : ℕ) : Type extends Flow NNReal (PhaseSpace n) where
  contDiff_space : ∀ t, ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (toFun t)
  continuous_fderiv :
    Continuous (fun p : NNReal × PhaseSpace n => fderiv ℝ (toFun p.1) p.2)

instance {n : ℕ} : CoeFun (SmoothSemiflow n)
    (fun _ => NNReal → PhaseSpace n → PhaseSpace n) :=
  ⟨fun φ => φ.toFun⟩

/-- A set is a global attractor if it is nonempty, compact, strictly invariant, and uniformly
attracts every bounded set: every bounded set is eventually mapped into every open neighborhood
of the attractor. -/
def IsGlobalAttractor {n : ℕ} (φ : SmoothSemiflow n) (K : Set (PhaseSpace n)) : Prop :=
  K.Nonempty ∧ IsCompact K ∧ (∀ t, φ t '' K = K) ∧
    ∀ B : Set (PhaseSpace n), IsBounded B → ∀ U : Set (PhaseSpace n), IsOpen U → K ⊆ U →
      ∀ᶠ t in atTop, MapsTo (φ t) B U

/-- Eden's infinite-time local Lyapunov dimension at `u`. It is the Kaplan--Yorke critical
order obtained from the limsup of
$\omega_d(D\varphi^t(u))^{1/t}$ as $t\to\infty$. -/
noncomputable def localLyapunovDimension {n : ℕ} (φ : SmoothSemiflow n)
    (u : PhaseSpace n) : ℝ :=
  sSup {d : ℝ | 0 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ n ∧
    1 ≤ limsup (fun t : NNReal =>
      if t = 0 then 0 else
        (singularValueFunction (fderiv ℝ (φ t) u) d) ^ ((t : ℝ)⁻¹)) atTop}

/-- A stationary point of a semiflow. -/
def IsEquilibrium {n : ℕ} (φ : SmoothSemiflow n) (u : PhaseSpace n) : Prop :=
  ∀ t, φ t u = u

/-- A point lies on a periodic orbit if it returns to itself after some positive time. -/
def LiesOnPeriodicOrbit {n : ℕ} (φ : SmoothSemiflow n) (u : PhaseSpace n) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : NNReal, 0 < T ∧ φ T u = u

/-- **Eden's conjecture:** for every smooth finite-dimensional dynamical system with compact global
attractor $K$, the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions on $K$ is attained at a point of $K$
which is either stationary or lies on a periodic orbit embedded in $K$. Here “unstable” in the
informal description of the periodic orbit is descriptive rather than an additional condition. -/
@[category research open, AMS 37]
theorem edens_conjecture {n : ℕ} (φ : SmoothSemiflow n) (K : Set (PhaseSpace n))
    (hK : IsGlobalAttractor φ K) :
    ∃ u ∈ K, (IsEquilibrium φ u ∨ LiesOnPeriodicOrbit φ u) ∧
      localLyapunovDimension φ u = sSup (localLyapunovDimension φ '' K) := by
  sorry

end EdensConjecture

/-!

Eden's conjecture states that the supremum of the local Lyapunov dimensions on the global
attractor of a smooth dynamical system is achieved on a stationary point or an unstable periodic
orbit embedded into the attractor. It was proposed by Alp Eden in 1987.

We follow the setting of Kuznetsov (2016). A smooth dynamical system is a semiflow
$\{\varphi^t\}_{t \ge 0}$ on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space whose time-$t$ maps are
continuously differentiable. For $u$ in the phase space and $t \ge 0$, let
$\sigma_1(t, u) \ge \dots \ge \sigma_n(t, u) \ge 0$ be the singular values of $D\varphi^t(u)$
and, for $d \in [0, n]$, let
$$\omega_d(D\varphi^t(u)) = \sigma_1(t, u) \cdots \sigma_{\lfloor d \rfloor}(t, u)\,
  \sigma_{\lfloor d \rfloor + 1}(t, u)^{d - \lfloor d \rfloor}$$
be the singular value function. The (infinite-time) local Lyapunov dimension of Eden at $u$ is
$$\dim_{\rm L}^{\rm E}(u) = \inf\{d \in [0, n] :
  \limsup_{t \to +\infty} \big(\omega_d(D\varphi^t(u))\big)^{1/t} < 1\},$$
with the convention that it equals $n$ when no such $d$ exists.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Eden's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- A. Eden, *An abstract theory of L-exponents with applications to dimension analysis*,
  PhD thesis, Indiana University (1989), p. 98, Question 1.
- A. Eden, *Local Lyapunov exponents and a local estimate of Hausdorff dimension*,
  Modélisation Mathématique et Analyse Numérique 23 (1989),

  Physics Letters A 380 (2016), [arXiv:1602.05410](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05410).
-/

largest eigenvalue of `A* A` for `i < n`, and `0` for `i ≥ n`. -/

  if h : i < Module.finrank ℝ E then

/-- A smooth finite-dimensional forward-time dynamical system. -/
def IsSmoothSemiflow {n : ℕ}
    (φ : NNReal → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  (∀ u, φ 0 u = u) ∧
  (∀ s t u, φ (s + t) u = φ s (φ t u)) ∧
  Continuous (fun p : NNReal × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => φ p.1 p.2) ∧
  ∀ t, ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (φ t)

/-- A compact invariant set which is minimal among bounded closed invariant sets attracting every
point of the phase space. -/
def IsGlobalAttractor {n : ℕ}
    (φ : NNReal → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  K.Nonempty ∧ IsCompact K ∧
  (∀ t, φ t '' K = K) ∧
  (∀ u, Tendsto (fun t => Metric.infDist (φ t u) K) atTop (nhds 0)) ∧

  Real.sqrt ((LinearMap.isSymmetric_adjoint_mul_self A.toLinearMap).eigenvalues (by simp) i)

/-- The singular-value function
`ω_d(A) = ∏ i, σ_i(A) ^ min(1, max(0, d - i))`. For `0 ≤ d ≤ n`, this is the
product of the first `⌊d⌋` singular values and the appropriate fractional power of the next one. -/
noncomputable def singularValueFunction {n : ℕ}
    (A : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (d : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n, Real.rpow (singularValue A i) (min 1 (max 0 (d - (i : ℕ))))

/-- Eden's infinite-time local growth of the singular-value function. -/
noncomputable def edenGrowthRate {n : ℕ}
    (φ : NNReal → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (d : ℝ) : ENNReal :=
  limsup (fun t : NNReal =>
    (ENNReal.ofReal (singularValueFunction (fderiv ℝ (φ t) u) d)).rpow (1 / (t : ℝ))) atTop

/-- Eden's infinite-time local Lyapunov dimension: the critical dimension determined by the
asymptotic singular-value growth. This is the Kaplan--Yorke value of the corresponding local
Lyapunov exponents. -/
noncomputable def localLyapunovDimension {n : ℕ}
    (φ : NNReal → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) : ℝ :=
  sSup {d : ℝ | 0 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ n ∧ 1 ≤ edenGrowthRate φ u d}

/-- A stationary point of a forward-time dynamical system. -/
def IsEquilibrium {n : ℕ}
    (φ : NNReal → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ t, φ t u = u

/-- A point lying on a periodic orbit of a forward-time dynamical system. -/
def IsPeriodicPoint {n : ℕ}
    (φ : NNReal → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : NNReal, 0 < T ∧ φ T u = u

/--
**Eden's conjecture.** For every smooth finite-dimensional dynamical system with a compact global
attractor $K$, the supremum of the infinite-time local Lyapunov dimensions on $K$ is attained at a
stationary point or on a periodic orbit embedded in $K$. The source describes the periodic orbit as
unstable; this is descriptive and is not imposed as an extra condition.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 37]
theorem edens_conjecture :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (φ : NNReal → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
      (K : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))),
      0 < n → IsSmoothSemiflow φ → IsGlobalAttractor φ K →
      ∃ u ∈ K, (IsEquilibrium φ u ∨ IsPeriodicPoint φ u) ∧
        IsGreatest (localLyapunovDimension φ '' K) (localLyapunovDimension φ u) := by
  sorry

end EdensConjecture
modeling_decisions: Modeled a smooth finite-dimensional dynamical system as a jointly continuous forward-time semiflow on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`, with every time map `ContDiff ℝ ⊤`; required `0 < n` to express the usual positive finite-dimensional phase space.
Used the background article's definition of a global attractor: a nonempty compact invariant set that attracts every point and is minimal among bounded closed invariant globally attractive sets.
Defined singular values from the decreasing eigenvalues of `A†A`, then defined the singular-value function `ω_d` by a uniform product formula valid for real `d ∈ [0,n]`.

Modeled Eden's infinite-time local Lyapunov dimension as the critical `d` determined by `limsup_{t→∞} ω_d(Dφ^t(u))^(1/t)`. This is the Eden/Constantin–Foias–Temam version discussed in arXiv:1602.05410 and is the critical-growth form of its Kaplan–Yorke formulation.
Used `ENNReal` for asymptotic growth so unbounded growth is represented by `⊤` rather than invoking the default behavior of a conditionally complete real-valued limsup.
Expressed attainment of the supremum by `IsGreatest (localLyapunovDimension φ '' K) ...`, which requires an actual maximizing point rather than merely an approximating sequence.

Treated “unstable” as descriptive, as directed by the decomposition: no extra instability predicate is imposed. Membership of the periodic point in `K`, together with invariance of `K`, makes its orbit embedded in the attractor.
A periodic point has a strictly positive period. Equilibria can also satisfy this periodicity predicate, but this does not change the union with the explicit equilibrium alternative.
